newsitem.title: USA: Glenayre to fight class action law suit.
newsitem.headline: Glenayre to fight class action law suit.

text.p: Glenayre Technologies Inc said on Thursday it planned to defend itself vigorously against a lawsuit filed against the company in early November alleging violations of U.S. securities law.

"The allegations referenced in the lawsuit are totally without merit, " Gary Smith, president and chief operating officer, said. "This law firm (representing the plaintiffs) has a history of preying on technology companies for its own personal gain and we intend to vigorously defend ourselves against them."
Glenayre said, while it had not been served notice of the suit, it became aware of it through a press release issued by Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach, attorneys for the plaintiff.

Glenayre shareholders filed a class action suit against the company in a U.S. District Court, alleging the company made numerous references to a firm order backlog when the backlog was not firm, plaintiff lawyers said on November 4.

Plaintiffs, who sought to recover damages, were represented by Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP, Bernstein Leibhard & Lifshitz, Savett Frutkin Podell & Ryand PC and the law offices of Bernard M. Gross, P.C.

This complaint, which alleged violations of the U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934, also alleged that Glenayre's share price was artificially inflated during the class period because of a series of materially false and misleading financial statements, the lawyers said.
The company said it obtained a copy of the complaint, filed against it and certain officers and directors, on November 4.
